seg.91bce9460ade.en: Kodi kura is the chicken curry that fills Andhra homes on a Sunday afternoon: bone-in chicken marinated in chilli and turmeric, cooked down in a gravy of deep-golden onions and tomatoes, and finished with garam masala. It goes to the table with hot rice, and the leftovers with dosa or chapati at night.

seg.2422ebb922bc.en: The heat here comes from our Teja chilli powder, the extra-hot Guntur chilli that gives Andhra curries their bite and bright red colour, with our turmeric powder in the marinade. This recipe serves 4 and is properly fiery; the tips say how to scale it down.

seg.d3855c7cad24.en: How to check turmeric powder at home

seg.3b01a30ec3ce.en: Rub the chicken with curd, Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Rest 30 minutes. Cover the bowl and keep it in the fridge while it rests.

seg.217eb90c7dac.en: Heat the oil in a heavy pan or kadai on medium heat. Add the cloves, cardamoms and cinnamon and let them sizzle for a few seconds.

seg.41164e7a534a.en: Add the onions, green chillies and curry leaves.

seg.127dbd26bc4d.en: Fry the onions in oil till deep golden. This takes 12–15 minutes on medium heat; stir often so they brown evenly without burning.

seg.3fa3e9f33095.en: Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomatoes, and cook till soft. Fry the paste for 1 minute until the raw smell goes, then cook the tomatoes for 5–6 minutes, mashing them, until they break down and oil shows at the edges.

seg.24dbd7dfd784.en: Stir in the coriander powder and fry for 30 seconds.

seg.461e7a0a9c22.en: Add the chicken and cook covered on medium heat till no pink remains near the bone. Fry it uncovered for the first 5 minutes until the pieces turn opaque, then pour in the hot water, cover and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then.

seg.22f96ed1f76e.en: Check a thick piece: the chicken is cooked when no pink remains near the bone and the juices run clear. Taste the gravy and add salt if needed.

seg.f10b1f5ae914.en: Stir in garam masala and coriander leaves. Simmer 3 minutes, uncovered, until the gravy is as thick as you like and a red film of oil floats on top.

seg.a7c73631b2ca.en: Switch off and rest the curry for 10 minutes before serving; the gravy settles and the flavour comes together.

seg.0b948e3072fa.en: Brown the onions deep golden; the gravy's colour and body come from them.

seg.e0365adcf1bf.en: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For a medium curry use 1 tsp, or use Sannam chilli powder for red colour with gentler heat.

seg.57940a63282d.en: Use bone-in pieces; the bones give the gravy its depth.

seg.4f9718c3bc6f.en: Let the oil separate from the tomato masala before the chicken goes in, or the gravy tastes raw.

seg.164627c386b7.en: Kobbari kodi kura: grind 3 tbsp grated coconut with 1 tbsp poppy seeds and a little water, and stir the paste in with the garam masala for a richer gravy.

seg.7d79f857440a.en: Ground masala: dry-roast 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp fennel seeds, 3 cloves and a small piece of cinnamon, grind, and use instead of the coriander powder and garam masala.

seg.ea1fd7a2c573.en: Pressure cooker: after adding the chicken and water, cook for 2 whistles and let the pressure drop on its own.

seg.8b4376996905.en: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, the Sunday way. It also goes well with chapati, dosa or ragi sangati.

seg.45cb0a9558e6.en: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat until steaming hot all the way through. The curry tastes deeper the next day.

seg.bc11ae48bfcf.en: How do I make Andhra chicken curry less spicy?

seg.aaa9ea580a50.en: Cut the Teja chilli powder to 1 tsp, or use Sannam chilli powder, which gives the same red colour with gentler heat. A spoon of curd stirred in at the end also softens the bite.

seg.fe399a2a853e.en: Why is Andhra chicken curry so spicy?

seg.ada87f188506.en: Andhra cooking uses Guntur chillies such as Teja, which are much hotter than the chilli powder used in most other regional curries. The heat is part of the dish.

seg.fc940ab96cce.en: How do I know the chicken is cooked through?

seg.1445f73d2fc1.en: Cut into the thickest piece near the bone. The chicken is cooked when no pink remains near the bone and the juices run clear.

seg.736c9b09bcd3.en: Can I make kodi kura without curd?

seg.f9ab2afc44b4.en: Yes. Marinate the chicken with the chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt and 1 tbsp lemon juice, and add one more tomato to the gravy.

seg.c9c11f5b43da.en: Bellam atukulu is the 10-minute sweet of Telugu homes. It is the poha offered to Krishna on Krishnashtami, recalling Kuchela's gift, and it is also a quick sweet for children after school. The poha is only rinsed, never cooked in water, and then tossed in warm jaggery syrup.

seg.8594fedb25dc.en: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery gives it a deep brown colour and a rich, slightly smoky sweetness. This recipe serves 2.

seg.fbe7b4b8afbc.en: Put the poha in a sieve and pick out any bits of husk.

seg.b0f730c0b062.en: Rinse the poha in a sieve under running water for a few seconds, drain, and leave it for 5 minutes to soften. It should feel soft when pressed, but not wet.

seg.0a3e2261d7bc.en: Grate the palm jaggery finely, breaking up any hard lumps.

seg.d2b892bf70af.en: Melt the palm jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it. Wipe the pan and pour the syrup back in.

seg.d073ead78aef.en: If you are using cashews, fry them in a little ghee till golden.

seg.62c17a0f01a5.en: Add the poha, coconut and cardamom to the warm syrup and toss gently on a low flame for 1–2 minutes, until every flake is coated. Use a light hand so the flakes do not break.

seg.d1abe3d7557d.en: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the flakes are coated; longer cooking makes them chewy.

seg.c91ffab6359d.en: Finish with the ghee and cashews. Serve warm or at room temperature.

seg.544ea222a497.en: Use thick poha. Thin poha turns mushy in the syrup.

seg.0f56d718ca89.en: Do not soak the poha in a bowl of water; a quick rinse is enough, or it turns soft and sticky.

seg.972f174730fe.en: Keep the syrup warm, not bubbling, when the poha goes in, so the flakes coat evenly.

seg.1797acff16a2.en: Cane jaggery: use the same amount of grated cane jaggery for a lighter colour and a caramel-like sweetness.

seg.8496cfe4aa1d.en: With milk: pour 2–3 tbsp warm milk over the finished poha for a softer sweet.

seg.bb5e4ee879e6.en: With sesame: add 1 tbsp roasted sesame seeds along with the coconut.

seg.25d7247d3c7b.en: Serve it as naivedyam on Krishnashtami, or as a quick sweet for children after school.

seg.1170385c1b79.en: Best eaten the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them the next day; the poha firms up as it stands.

seg.6acb206e9df4.en: Which poha is best for bellam atukulu?

seg.7cb97f8423cf.en: Thick poha (atukulu). It holds its shape in the warm syrup; thin poha turns mushy.

seg.ba8eb1721096.en: Can I make bellam atukulu with cane jaggery?

seg.2a1aa941db07.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery (cheruku bellam). It turns lighter in colour, with a caramel-like sweetness.

seg.88008fa2d0e6.en: Why is my bellam atukulu sticky?

seg.a6945e480c9a.en: The poha was soaked or cooked too long. Rinse it for only a few seconds, and take the pan off the heat as soon as every flake is coated.

seg.d4c0fab65bf7.en: Why is it made on Krishnashtami?

seg.51ab1914ac8d.en: It recalls the story of Kuchela, who brought a handful of poha to his friend Krishna as his only gift.

seg.b79702dac541.en: Bellam pongali is the sweet pongal that Telugu homes cook on Sankranti morning: rice and roasted moong dal cooked very soft, then sweetened with jaggery and enriched with ghee. It is offered as naivedyam before the festive meal, and it is also the prasadam at many temples and Friday pujas.

seg.17053455adbb.en: Cane jaggery gives it a light brown colour and a round, toffee-like sweetness, and ghee-fried whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack add the crunch. This recipe serves 4.

seg.a6184e3e789c.en: Roast the moong dal till light golden, then cook it with the rice till very soft and mushy. Start by dry-roasting the dal in a pressure cooker or heavy-bottomed pot on low heat, stirring, until it smells nutty and turns light golden, about 3–4 minutes.

seg.03597768c72a.en: Add the rice to the roasted dal, wash both together in 2–3 changes of water, and drain.

seg.1c139f802ab6.en: Add the 3 cups water. Pressure cook for 4–5 whistles on medium heat and let the pressure drop on its own, or simmer covered in a pot for 25–30 minutes, adding a splash of hot water if it dries out.

seg.5c9fcb8182ea.en: Open and mash the rice and dal lightly with the back of a ladle. It should be soft and porridge-like, not dry.

seg.41870045e57c.en: Melt the jaggery in ¼ cup water and pour it into the rice. Warm the jaggery and water in a small pan on low heat, stirring, just until it dissolves, about 2–3 minutes; it does not need to boil.

seg.ca9ed938d301.en: Simmer, stirring, till thick and glossy, 5–7 minutes; stir in 2 tbsp ghee. Keep the heat low and stir all the way to the bottom, as the pongali catches easily once the jaggery is in.

seg.58e11747230d.en: Taste, and stir in a little more melted jaggery if you want it sweeter.

seg.9eabfb77c3db.en: Fry the cashews in the rest of the ghee; add with the cardamom. Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan on medium-low heat and stir the cashews until golden, about 1 minute, adding the raisins for the last few seconds until they puff up.

seg.4f12a8dd8723.en: Pour the cashews, raisins and ghee over the pongali, sprinkle in the cardamom powder and the camphor, if using, and stir well.

seg.25eb1725b7f2.en: Switch off and serve warm. Pongali thickens as it stands; loosen it with a few spoons of hot water if needed.

seg.d8d20508ad3b.en: Cook the rice and dal fully soft; they stop softening once the jaggery goes in.

seg.c5408f916731.en: Roasting the moong dal gives pongali its nutty smell; keep the heat low so it turns golden, not brown.

seg.5ed9375ff107.en: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and keep stirring once the jaggery is in; it catches and burns quickly.

seg.92b31a616baa.en: Take the pongali off the heat while it is still a little loose; it sets as it cools.

seg.1c14403a599f.en: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for a darker pongali with a deeper, smoky sweetness.

seg.d1a4e19c923c.en: Chakkera pongali: use ¾ cup sugar in place of the jaggery for a pale, sugar-sweet version.

seg.cd25d9fb2a56.en: Coconut: fry 2 tbsp thin slivers of dry coconut in the ghee along with the cashews.

seg.44acc6e45d4b.en: Offer it as naivedyam on Sankranti morning, then serve it warm with the festive meal, alongside pulihora and garelu.

seg.b4e15a70f8c8.en: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm with a splash of hot water and a little ghee, stirring, before serving.

seg.70c91f153ba8.en: What is the difference between pongali and chakkera pongali?

seg.75f25d8f552a.en: Pongali on its own often means the savoury version made with pepper and cumin. Chakkera pongali and bellam pongali are the sweet versions, made with sugar or jaggery.

seg.94d3b2adcbef.en: Can I make bellam pongali in a pressure cooker?

seg.269aace6e2a8.en: Yes. Cook the roasted dal and rice with 3 cups water for 4–5 whistles, let the pressure drop on its own, then add the melted jaggery and simmer in the open cooker.

seg.cd439685b7b5.en: Why did my pongali turn hard after cooling?

seg.696811a7ce7d.en: Pongali sets as it cools, and simmering too long after the jaggery goes in makes it firmer. Take it off while it is still a little loose, and loosen leftovers with hot water.

seg.b0499dbc1bd0.en: Can I use palm jaggery for pongali?

seg.7ee832015d30.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The pongali turns darker and tastes deeper and slightly smoky.

seg.0fff539adaed.en: Chepala pulusu is the tamarind fish curry of coastal Andhra, made with special care in the Godavari districts: thick fish steaks simmered in a sour, red tamarind gravy with onions, green chillies and curry leaves. It is a Sunday lunch dish, and many homes cook it in a clay pot and keep it for the next day, when the gravy has soaked into the fish.

seg.17fc336d9c12.en: Our turmeric powder goes into the marinade and the gravy. Sannam chilli powder gives the pulusu its deep red colour and a steady heat that balances the tamarind. This recipe serves 4.

seg.2fafef6b8781.en: Wash the fish pieces gently in water two or three times and drain them well.

seg.cf370c2b1459.en: Rub the fish with salt, turmeric and 1 tsp chilli powder; rest 15 minutes. Use 1 tsp salt and ¼ tsp of the turmeric powder for the marinade.

seg.0c7defd6c85a.en: Squeeze the soaked tamarind well in its water and strain it. You should have about 2 cups of thin tamarind water.

seg.a8777ed4c461.en: Heat the oil in a wide pan or clay pot on medium heat. Add the fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds and cumin seeds and let them splutter, taking care that the fenugreek does not turn dark.

seg.e87b5c1bcc02.en: Fry the onions, chillies and curry leaves in oil till soft; add the spice powders. Fry the onions about 6–8 minutes until soft and light golden, add the ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook 2 minutes, then add the remaining turmeric powder, the remaining Sannam chilli powder and the coriander powder and stir for 30 seconds.

seg.61e849535fa9.en: Pour in the tamarind water and boil 10 minutes till the oil rises. Add the salt for the gravy; the raw tamarind smell should be gone and the gravy slightly thick.

seg.65cb3d6833cd.en: Taste the gravy. It should be clearly sour, salty and hot, as the fish will take in some of it.

seg.fc6f288cacf9.en: Slide in the fish and simmer covered 10–12 minutes; swirl, do not stir. Lay the pieces in one layer, spoon gravy over them and keep the heat low.

seg.9fed4db6e81b.en: Check one piece at the thickest part: the fish is cooked when the flesh is white or opaque right through and comes away from the bone easily.

seg.8a5166c34dc3.en: Sprinkle the coriander leaves, switch off and let the pulusu rest at least 30 minutes, covered, before serving.

seg.c6819a9980cc.en: Swirl the pan instead of stirring so the fish stays whole.

seg.1333bb67a0a8.en: Pick a firm fish with thick steaks; thin fillets break up in the long simmer.

seg.dd6f5d867621.en: Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat. Use 1½ tbsp for a milder pulusu, or the full 2 tbsp for the usual Andhra heat.

seg.6196c7ae078f.en: Boil the tamarind gravy well before the fish goes in; once the fish is in, you cannot cook it much longer without it breaking.

seg.cadf91d0b4a1.en: Teja chilli powder: for a hotter pulusu, use 1 tbsp Teja chilli powder in place of the Sannam in the gravy. Teja is very hot; start with 2 tsp if unsure.

seg.1639b09f9df2.en: Royyala pulusu: use 400 g cleaned prawns and simmer only 5–6 minutes, until they turn pink and curl.

seg.f5f2c78097e7.en: Mamidikaya pulusu: in summer, Godavari homes add slices of raw mango and use less tamarind.

seg.4bb7dd4c2c98.en: Serve with hot steamed rice and sliced onions. Many Godavari homes serve it the next day, when the flavours have settled.

seg.6efbfa504170.en: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in the pan without stirring, until steaming hot all the way through.

seg.3fb4609a3953.en: Which fish is best for chepala pulusu?

seg.379b410c6994.en: Firm river or sea fish cut into thick steaks: rohu, catla (bochcha), murrel (korameenu) or seer fish. Bony small fish also work but need gentle handling.

seg.1d2170a88905.en: Why does chepala pulusu taste better the next day?

seg.566bd302c316.en: Resting gives the fish time to soak up the tamarind and chilli gravy, and the sourness and heat even out. That is why many homes cook it in the morning for dinner or the next day.

seg.53fa2d1b73d6.en: How do I stop the fish from breaking in the curry?

seg.adc2b712af00.en: Use thick steaks, add them only after the gravy has boiled, keep the heat low and swirl the pan instead of stirring with a spoon.

seg.9f483b378e98.en: How much tamarind for 500 g fish?

seg.f77f33d6b7c5.en: About 40 g, a lemon-sized ball, soaked in 2 cups of warm water. Use a little less if you add tomato or raw mango.

seg.4fea7db714b7.en: Chimmili is a small Telugu sweet of roasted sesame and jaggery, ground coarsely and rolled into balls. It is one of the offerings made on Nagula Chavithi in Karthika masam, along with chalimidi and the milk poured at the snake anthill (putta). Sesame and jaggery sweets like it are made again at Sankranti.

seg.6e104d560e56.en: Roasted sesame gives it a nutty, toasty taste, and cane jaggery a caramel sweetness. The texture is soft and a little crumbly, and each ball is gone in two bites. This recipe makes about 12.

seg.39c46fb56757.en: 1 tsp ghee, for greasing your palms

seg.ed775cba4fcf.en: Grate the jaggery and measure out the sesame before you start; once the sesame is roasted, the rest moves quickly.

seg.cfb9d281b47f.en: Heat a heavy kadai or pan on low heat for a minute. Add the sesame; no oil or ghee is needed.

seg.89a51ce5355c.en: Dry-roast the sesame on a low flame till it crackles and turns light golden. Stir all the time; the seeds start to pop and smell nutty after 4–6 minutes. Do not let them turn brown.

seg.999792547560.en: Tip the sesame onto a wide plate straight away so it stops browning. Cool it for about 5 minutes, until it is just warm to the touch.

seg.77b614ea2f92.en: Grind the sesame coarsely in short pulses. Use the small jar of the mixer and pulse 3–4 times, a second or two at a time; stop while you can still see broken seeds.

seg.175aeced5810.en: Add the jaggery and cardamom; pulse till it comes together. This takes 4–6 more short pulses; scrape down the sides once. A pinch pressed between your fingers should hold its shape.

seg.6f94cb46b9ab.en: If the mixture is too dry to hold, add 1–2 tsp more grated jaggery and pulse once or twice again.

seg.226f137c9449.en: Tip the mixture into a bowl and grease your palms lightly with ghee.

seg.ff3eb71729c2.en: Shape into small balls. Take a heaped tablespoon at a time, press it firmly in your fist, then roll it smooth. Work quickly while the mixture is still warm, as it turns crumbly when it cools.

seg.ee9e027268aa.en: Leave the balls on a plate until they cool completely, about 15 minutes, then store them in an airtight jar.

seg.7fe633314020.en: Roast on a low flame and keep stirring; sesame goes from golden to burnt quickly, and burnt sesame tastes bitter.

seg.d50b37351252.en: Grind in short pulses only; long runs turn sesame into an oily paste.

seg.75f5428655c4.en: Shape while the mixture is warm. If it turns crumbly, pulse it once more with a teaspoon of grated jaggery.

seg.1d42a24453d2.en: Soft jaggery binds best. If yours is hard, grate it finely so it blends in evenly.

seg.5a7ed16f4810.en: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for darker chimmili with a smoky sweetness.

seg.569a63f3cd17.en: Black sesame (nalla nuvvulu): roast and grind it the same way for darker, stronger-tasting balls.

seg.da0d1a9b6378.en: Peanut or coconut: pulse in 2 tbsp roasted peanuts or grated dry coconut with the jaggery.

seg.32d41fc0994e.en: Without a mixer: pound the warm sesame and jaggery together in a stone mortar (rolu) until the mixture holds, then shape.

seg.2fa9aaef4425.en: On Nagula Chavithi morning, offer chimmili with milk at the snake anthill (putta) or in your puja, then share them as prasadam. They also go well with evening tea.

seg.bd50831bbb3f.en: Keeps a week in an airtight jar. Store the jar at room temperature, in a dry place.

seg.4023b0de08bd.en: Why is my chimmili not holding together?

seg.7fed90d1ebe0.en: The sesame may be under-ground, or the mixture may have cooled. Pulse it once more with 1–2 tsp extra grated jaggery and shape it while it is still warm.

seg.694d2b416f39.en: Why does my chimmili taste bitter?

seg.d0ee77d0957e.en: The sesame was roasted too dark. Roast it on a low flame only until it crackles and turns light golden, then tip it onto a plate at once so it stops browning.

seg.30d31a37acfa.en: Can I use palm jaggery instead of cane jaggery?

seg.77afe99f558c.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The chimmili will be darker, with a deeper, slightly smoky sweetness.

seg.bae4fc214e74.en: Nagula Chavithi falls on Friday, 13 November 2026, in Karthika masam, a few days after Deepavali. Chimmili, chalimidi and milk are among the offerings made at the snake anthill (putta) that morning.

seg.fabe2a976262.en: Gongura mamsam is mutton cooked with gongura, the sour sorrel leaf that Andhra, and Guntur above all, treats as its own. The mutton is cooked soft with chilli and turmeric, then simmered with gongura that has been sauteed down to a dark, tangy paste, until the curry is thick and the oil rises to the top.

seg.a26e996a46c7.en: Gongura's sharp sourness needs strong heat to stand up to it, and that comes from our Teja chilli powder, the extra-hot Guntur chilli, with our turmeric powder alongside. Serves 4 with rice.

seg.c89b5d92359a.en: Put the mutton in a pressure cooker with the Teja chilli powder, turmeric powder, ginger-garlic paste and salt, mix well and leave for 15 minutes.

seg.d7a27bd7d1d5.en: Pressure-cook the mutton with Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, salt and water. Add the 1½ cups water and cook for 5–6 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure drop on its own.

seg.c084351b01db.en: Open the cooker and check a piece: the mutton is done when it is tender and pulls away from the bone easily with a spoon. If not, cook for 1–2 more whistles.

seg.80af0da3b5a1.en: While the mutton cooks, heat the 1 tbsp oil in a pan on medium heat.

seg.c59d6a34def2.en: Saute the gongura with green chillies in a little oil till it melts to a dark paste. This takes 8–10 minutes; stir often and mash the leaves with the back of the spoon as they wilt.

seg.37056d0dd9cf.en: Heat the 4 tbsp oil in a heavy kadai on medium heat and add the cloves, cardamoms and cinnamon.

seg.26a945a9fad3.en: Fry the onions with whole spices till golden. Add the curry leaves with the onions, and give them 10–12 minutes, stirring often.

seg.4dd72cc1abd0.en: Stir in the coriander powder and fry for 30 seconds. Add the mutton and its stock, then the gongura.

seg.46f5f6c735ac.en: Simmer till thick and the oil floats on top. Keep the heat low, stir now and then, and allow 12–15 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt now, once the sourness of the gongura is in.

seg.0abf0f798bd3.en: Stir in garam masala. Cook 2 more minutes, then switch off and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

seg.c57eb6bfb001.en: Taste after the gongura goes in; its sourness varies from bunch to bunch.

seg.5544823d42b4.en: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For medium heat use 1 tsp, or Sannam chilli powder; do not cut it out entirely, or the gongura tastes flat and sour.

seg.62683a58a9fd.en: Do not use an aluminium pan for the gongura; its sourness reacts with the metal and darkens the curry. Use steel or cast iron.

seg.d036336075e5.en: If the gongura is very sour, add 1 more onion to the masala to balance it.

seg.8faa3986eaa2.en: Gongura chicken: use 750 g bone-in chicken, skip the pressure cooker and cook it covered in the masala for 20–25 minutes, until no pink remains near the bone, before the gongura goes in.

seg.2ebce7872a6e.en: Gongura royyalu: use 500 g cleaned prawns, add them after the onions and cook 5–6 minutes, just until they turn pink and curl, then add the gongura.

seg.7f3c45600b1c.en: Red chilli gongura: fry 6 dried red chillies with the gongura and grind them together for a darker, sharper curry.

seg.6fc7d7ad8ce1.en: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with jonna rotte. A plain raw onion on the side is the Guntur way.

seg.a4e072616940.en: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat until steaming hot all the way through. Like most sour curries, it tastes better the next day.

seg.50430ec58f61.en: Gongura is sorrel leaves, also called roselle or red sorrel (ambadi in Marathi, pitwa in Hindi). The leaves are sour and cook down to a dark paste.

seg.c813168eb832.en: Can I use gongura pickle instead of gongura leaves?

seg.e1453431b91a.en: Yes, in a pinch. Stir in 3–4 tbsp gongura pickle in place of the sauteed leaves and cut down the salt and chilli powder, since the pickle already has both.

seg.13ee618e3c36.en: How long should I pressure-cook mutton for gongura mamsam?

seg.5888ba63831a.en: About 5–6 whistles on medium heat for bone-in curry-cut mutton. It is done when the meat pulls away from the bone easily; older mutton may need 1–2 more whistles.

seg.5f47c430018f.en: How do I make gongura mutton less spicy?

seg.e4fe5fb9cf48.en: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder or swap in Sannam chilli powder, and use 2 green chillies. Keep some heat, as it balances the sourness of the gongura.

seg.a7dd4a4d025c.en: Gongura pachadi is the chutney Andhra is best known for: sour gongura (sorrel) leaves fried down in oil and ground with roasted spices, garlic and red chilli. Around Guntur and Palnadu it is on the table almost every day, mixed into hot rice with a spoon of ghee, with sliced onion on the side.

seg.73ddd8b1df98.en: Teja chilli powder gives it the deep red colour and the sharp heat that stands up to the sourness of the leaves. This recipe makes about 1½ cups, enough for 6.

seg.b4b21c43d6d9.en: Fry gongura leaves in oil till they turn to a dark mash, then grind them with roasted coriander, fenugreek, garlic, Teja chilli powder and salt. Finish with a mustard and dal tempering.

seg.69e8fc35d187.en: Pick the gongura leaves off the stems and wash them in 2–3 changes of water. Spread them on a cloth and pat them completely dry; water left on the leaves splutters in the oil and shortens how long the pachadi keeps.

seg.1b214adb5a9c.en: Roast the coriander, cumin and fenugreek till fragrant; let them cool. Use a dry pan on low heat and stir all the time: the fenugreek should turn one shade darker, about 2 minutes, but not brown.

seg.6dd2ecdfbc2f.en: Fry the gongura leaves in 1 tbsp oil till they wilt to a dark mash, 6–8 minutes. Use a wide pan on medium heat and stir often; the leaves shrink fast, turn from green to a dull olive-brown, and almost all their water cooks off.

seg.adc2540067f6.en: Spread the leaves on a plate and let them cool completely, about 10 minutes.

seg.78d34fa0267e.en: Grind the spices with the garlic, chilli powder and salt, then pulse in the leaves. Grind the roasted spices, the 6 garlic cloves, Teja chilli powder and salt to a coarse powder first.

seg.e84cadbb2f28.en: Add the cooled leaves and pulse 3–4 times to a coarse paste, without any water. Many Andhra homes pound it in a stone mortar (rolu) instead.

seg.c04597c43292.en: Taste: it should be sour, hot and well salted. Add a pinch more salt if the sourness feels too sharp.

seg.317793f8bd6d.en: Temper mustard, dals, red chillies and curry leaves in the rest of the oil; mix it in. Heat the 2 tbsp sesame oil in a small pan, let the mustard seeds crackle, fry the chana dal and urad dal till golden, then add the red chillies, crushed garlic, curry leaves and asafoetida for a few seconds. Pour it over the pachadi and stir well.

seg.bd6dcf672985.en: Let the pachadi sit for 30 minutes if you can, so the flavours come together, then spoon it into a clean, dry glass jar.

seg.e0bb74b2a966.en: Dry the leaves fully before frying so the pachadi keeps longer.

seg.29688dc9fded.en: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For a milder pachadi use 1 tsp, or half Teja and half Sannam chilli powder.

seg.d1fa39431c01.en: Keep the fenugreek to ¼ tsp and roast it only one shade darker; more, or darker, makes the pachadi bitter.

seg.00435dc24e2d.en: Pulse, do not grind smooth: gongura pachadi should be coarse, with bits of leaf you can see.

seg.70ea8f84244b.en: Do not skimp on the oil; the layer of oil on top helps the pachadi keep.

seg.bd2018335c09.en: With onion: stir 1 small onion, finely chopped, into a portion just before serving, and eat it the same day.

seg.77f8d979d9c5.en: Whole red chillies: in place of the chilli powder, fry 12–15 dried red chillies in a little oil and grind them with the spices.

seg.98bf90687f81.en: Green chilli gongura: fry 6–8 green chillies with the leaves and cut the chilli powder to 1 tsp, for a sharper, greener heat.

seg.3ffc938ce36f.en: Mix a spoon into hot rice with ghee and eat with sliced raw onion on the side. It also goes well with dosa, idli and as a side on any Andhra meal plate.

seg.9b58b3a03e55.en: Keep it in a clean, dry glass jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, always using a dry spoon. A thin layer of oil on top helps it keep.

seg.5fb383e7c1ab.en: What is gongura called in English?

seg.100f275734bd.en: Gongura is the leaf of the roselle plant, often sold as sorrel leaves or red sorrel. In Hindi- and Marathi-speaking areas it is called ambadi.

seg.7f27f7848f6b.en: How do I make gongura pachadi less sour?

seg.a8b5b3cafa35.en: Add a little more salt and chilli, or stir in 1 tsp grated jaggery. Frying the leaves down well also mellows their sourness.

seg.5bc83cd0bb23.en: Why is my gongura pachadi bitter?

seg.bcbd736912c5.en: Usually too much fenugreek, or fenugreek roasted too dark. Keep it to ¼ tsp and stop roasting when it is one shade darker.

seg.f5ec54c6b341.en: How long does gongura pachadi last?

seg.693b158b80df.en: About 2 weeks in the fridge in a dry glass jar, if the leaves were dried well and you always use a dry spoon. Outside the fridge, eat it within 2–3 days.

seg.dd0da0936d87.en: Kodi guddu pulusu is the Andhra egg curry that many homes make when there is no meat in the house: hard-boiled eggs simmered in a tangy gravy of tamarind and slow-fried onions. It is thinner and sourer than a North Indian egg curry, made to be mixed into plenty of hot rice.

seg.27588d5a0d73.en: Our Sannam chilli powder gives the pulusu its red colour and a steady medium heat, and our turmeric powder (Pasupu) gives the golden base. A little jaggery rounds off the sourness.

seg.4b88dbe5eb6d.en: Soak the tamarind in the warm water for 15 minutes. Squeeze it well, strain and keep the tamarind water; discard the fibres and seeds.

seg.e7eefe0a36b0.en: Boil the eggs 10 minutes, peel them and make 3–4 shallow slits on each. Start them in room-temperature water, count 10 minutes from the boil, then cool them in water before peeling. The yolk should be firm and pale yellow right through.

seg.6747ea35bd7d.en: Optional: heat 1 tsp of the oil with the pinch of turmeric and roll the eggs in it for 2 minutes until lightly blistered. Keep aside.

seg.9d3c50e45f8b.en: Heat the rest of the oil in a kadai on medium heat. Add the fenugreek seeds and let them turn light brown; they turn bitter if they go dark.

seg.c867d4469da7.en: Fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves and onions in the oil till soft and golden. Add the mustard seeds first and let them splutter, then the curry leaves, green chillies and asafoetida, then the onions for about 8 minutes.

seg.ae0272dd2475.en: Turn the heat to low. Add the turmeric, Sannam chilli powder and salt, then the tamarind water; simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the coriander powder with the chilli powder so it fries for a few seconds first.

seg.01aeed8b749f.en: The raw tamarind smell should be gone and the gravy should look glossy. Add ½ cup water if it thickens too fast.

seg.74f1a1affff6.en: Slide in the eggs and simmer 5 minutes more till the gravy thickens. Spoon the gravy over the eggs now and then.

seg.299781c49104.en: Stir in the jaggery, taste and adjust the salt or sourness, and scatter the coriander leaves.

seg.d0ce3c2b157a.en: Switch off and let the pulusu rest for 10 minutes before serving so the eggs take on the gravy.

seg.feebbb94999b.en: Slits let the tangy gravy into the eggs.

seg.98394356bb39.en: Cool the boiled eggs in water before peeling; the shells come off cleanly.

seg.f4306708f8c5.en: Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat; for a hotter pulusu add ½ tsp Teja chilli powder along with it.

seg.fc1643db807e.en: Pulusu tastes better after it rests, and even more the next day, as the eggs soak up the tamarind.

seg.b19fe3919add.en: Tomato: add 1 chopped tomato after the onions for a softer, less sour gravy.

seg.0d78d434249e.en: Sesame: stir in 1 tbsp roasted sesame powder in the last 5 minutes for a thicker, nutty gravy.

seg.e4adab31c02b.en: Mamidikaya: in summer, replace half the tamarind with a few pieces of raw mango cooked in the gravy.

seg.bbf897873153.en: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, with a crisp fry or appadalu on the side. It also goes with chapati or dosa.

seg.3af5b68fc2e1.en: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm the pulusu in a pan with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.

seg.3dae693db30c.en: How long should I boil eggs for egg curry?

seg.2d6d1a298a24.en: About 10 minutes from the time the water boils. The yolk should be firm and pale yellow right through, with no runny centre, before the eggs go into the gravy.

seg.4abaae123f39.en: Why do you make slits on eggs for pulusu?

seg.d3f5992ccd6e.en: Shallow slits let the tamarind gravy soak into the egg white. Without them the gravy stays on the surface and the egg tastes plain.

seg.7a591bf728ac.en: How do I reduce the sourness of the pulusu?

seg.0a2bf657f386.en: Simmer it a few minutes longer, add a teaspoon of grated jaggery, or stir in a little water. Use a smaller ball of tamarind next time.

seg.f9a34864523d.en: What is the difference between egg pulusu and egg curry?

seg.08bcae4f5075.en: Pulusu is a thinner, tangy tamarind gravy made to mix with rice. A regular egg curry is usually built on onion and tomato, with no tamarind and a thicker masala.

seg.00fde8f92a7e.en: Gutti vankaya kura is the stuffed brinjal curry that Andhra homes make for Sunday lunches, weddings and when guests come over. Small, round purple brinjals are slit, packed with a roasted peanut, sesame and coconut masala, and cooked slowly in oil until they turn soft and the masala clings to them.

seg.27fd58488499.en: Our Sannam chilli powder gives the stuffing its red colour and medium heat, and turmeric powder rounds it off. Serve it with hot rice or chapati. This recipe serves 4.

seg.d56e638c12d0.en: Dry-roast the peanuts, sesame, coconut and coriander seeds; grind with the spices. Roast the peanuts first on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, then add the coriander seeds, cumin and sesame for 1 minute, and the coconut for the last 30 seconds, until it is light golden. Let it cool.

seg.26e4a965b3f7.en: In a mixer, grind the roasted mix with the garlic, Sannam chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt and tamarind to a coarse powder without water. It should clump when pressed.

seg.5784e45d4bff.en: Wash the brinjals and trim the green cap a little, leaving the stalk on.

seg.02665f13e5af.en: Slit each brinjal in a cross from the bottom, keeping the stem on, and pack in the stuffing. Cut about three-quarters of the way up so the four quarters stay joined at the top. Drop each one into a bowl of salted water as you go, then drain.

seg.498fc880430b.en: Press about 1 heaped tsp of stuffing into each brinjal. Keep the leftover stuffing aside.

seg.3daa0935ccba.en: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan on medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and, when they splutter, the curry leaves and onion, if using. Fry the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.

seg.3a140b72d6a0.en: Place the stuffed brinjals in a single layer in the pan.

seg.1ae98f10b6ed.en: Cook the brinjals in hot oil, covered, on a low flame, turning gently every 4–5 minutes. Use a spoon or tongs so the stuffing stays in, and cook for 15–18 minutes, until the skins wrinkle.

seg.50530663a626.en: Add the leftover stuffing with ½ cup water; simmer till the brinjals are soft. Cover and cook on low for 8–10 minutes more, until the masala thickens and oil shows at the sides.

seg.2a2726cfebd5.en: Check doneness: a knife should slide through the thickest brinjal with no resistance. Sprinkle the coriander leaves and switch off.

seg.c2e59cef6130.en: Keep the stalks on so the brinjals hold together while they cook and turn.

seg.15314c3b05cd.en: Pick small, glossy brinjals of the same size, so they cook evenly; large ones stay hard in the centre.

seg.208cff8b9d46.en: Roast the peanuts and sesame on medium-low heat; burnt sesame makes the whole masala bitter.

seg.7779355bd06d.en: For a milder curry, use 1½ tsp Sannam chilli powder; for more heat, go up to 1 tbsp.

seg.742d7eb81437.en: With onion masala: grind 1 small onion into the stuffing for a softer, slightly sweet gravy.

seg.abde9958c7fa.en: Without coconut: leave out the coconut and use 1 tbsp more peanuts and sesame.

seg.b9a6b34c8c73.en: Gravy style: add 1 cup water in place of ½ cup in the last step for a thinner curry to mix into rice.

seg.80faf3a5e4b1.en: Serve hot with steamed rice and a spoon of ghee, or with chapati or jonna rotte.

seg.9adac1f51f99.en: Keep covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. Warm gently with a splash of water.

seg.83ffeb71bb2a.en: Which brinjals are best for gutti vankaya?

seg.76c81f4beef2.en: Small, round purple brinjals about the size of an egg, with a glossy skin and green stalk. They cook through in the time the masala takes and hold the stuffing well.

seg.71325f387d2a.en: How do I know the brinjals are cooked?

seg.c65656faa952.en: The skins wrinkle and soften, and a knife slides through the thickest brinjal with no resistance. Undercooked brinjals feel firm and spongy in the centre.

seg.297ebd94e89c.en: Can I make gutti vankaya without coconut?

seg.f9ad1045b4c1.en: Yes. Use 1 tbsp more peanuts and 1 tbsp more sesame seeds in place of the coconut; the masala tastes nuttier.

seg.534e126ba995.en: Why do my brinjals fall apart?

seg.96bfe0b8ed06.en: The stalk was removed or the cross was cut all the way through. Keep the stalk on, stop the slit about a quarter from the top and turn them gently.

seg.111c74722b7d.en: Jeedipappu pakodi is the cashew pakoda that Andhra sweet shops and homes fry for tea time, festivals and guests: whole cashews in a thin, spiced coat of besan and rice flour, fried till crisp. Made without onion, it keeps for days in a jar, so many homes fry a batch for Diwali and Sankranti visitors.

seg.b4f22aebea20.en: Whole cashews from our Jeedipappu pack stay crunchy inside the coating, and Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat and a warm red colour. This recipe serves 4.

seg.8423a6481648.en: Rinse the cashews and drain them well; a slightly damp surface helps the flour stick.

seg.0d03259dc451.en: Heat the oil for deep frying in a kadai on medium heat.

seg.c7fa1a156718.en: Mix the besan, rice flour, chilli powder, salt, ginger-garlic paste and curry leaves. Use a wide bowl, and add the green chillies, coriander leaves and asafoetida at the same time.

seg.346911fb291b.en: Rub in 1 tbsp hot oil, add the cashews and sprinkle water till the flour just coats them. Spoon the hot oil from the kadai with care and rub it into the flour mix with your fingertips first, then add the cashews and sprinkle the water 1 tbsp at a time, tossing, until the flour clings to every cashew. The mix should look like damp crumbs, not a batter.

seg.05a50e3b5ae8.en: Check the oil: a pinch of the mix dropped in should rise to the top in 2–3 seconds with steady bubbles. If it browns at once, the oil is too hot.

seg.f3e77b6c0f73.en: Drop small clusters into medium-hot oil. Pick up 3–4 coated cashews at a time with your fingers and let them fall loosely into the oil, without crowding the kadai.

seg.5e4bfdad4c05.en: Fry, turning, till golden and crisp, 5–6 minutes; drain on paper. The bubbles around the pakodi get smaller and slow down when they are done.

seg.eb1a58e02e89.en: Fry the rest in batches the same way, letting the oil come back to heat between batches.

seg.8ab193492427.en: Let the pakodi rest for 5 minutes on the paper; they crisp up further as they cool. Sprinkle a pinch of salt or chilli powder over the top, if you like.

seg.c8ded38fad10.en: Keep the batter thick and dry, not runny, or the pakodi turns soft.

seg.9670def7c10b.en: Fry on medium heat: cashews brown fast, and on high heat the coating colours before the cashew inside is toasted.

seg.76602f605fc8.en: The spoon of hot oil rubbed into the flour makes the pakodi light and crisp.

seg.2494998e92ed.en: Sannam chilli powder gives a medium heat and a good red colour; use ½ tsp for children.

seg.7f70d313349e.en: Hotter: replace half the Sannam chilli powder with Teja chilli powder, which is much hotter.

seg.2b2be3846a1d.en: With onion: add 1 small onion, thinly sliced, with the cashews for a softer, sweeter pakodi, and eat it the same day.

seg.7f852eddc8b5.en: Mint: add 2 tbsp chopped mint leaves along with the coriander leaves.

seg.cd47edc05460.en: Serve warm with evening tea or filter coffee. They also go into lunch boxes or onto the side of a rice-and-pappu meal.

seg.e2777b4dabb7.en: Once fully cooled, keep them in an airtight jar at room temperature and eat within 4–5 days. If they soften, warm them in a dry pan on low heat for 2–3 minutes.

seg.f8c9120f7f67.en: Why did my cashew pakodi turn soft?

seg.346050614d3a.en: Too much water in the flour, or frying on low heat. Keep the mix like damp crumbs and fry on medium heat until the bubbles slow down.

seg.921421ebf2c6.en: Should I soak cashews before making pakodi?

seg.e6e487728264.en: No soak is needed. A quick rinse is enough to help the flour stick; cashews soaked for long lose some of their crunch.

seg.905443e515e2.en: Can I make cashew pakodi without rice flour?

seg.72a2c55cca9c.en: Yes. Use 2 tbsp more besan, or 1 tbsp cornflour. Rice flour gives the crispest coating, so the pakodi will be a little softer without it.

seg.f129edc737b1.en: How long does cashew pakodi stay crisp?

seg.d73ef4b28b6d.en: About 4–5 days in an airtight jar, as long as it cools completely before it goes in.

seg.a64f3158d8da.en: Upma is the everyday Andhra tiffin: semolina cooked soft in a seasoned water with onion, green chillies and curry leaves. Jeedipappu upma is the dressed-up version, with a good handful of cashews fried golden in ghee, the way it is made for guests, for festival mornings and at weddings, often served next to pesarattu or with a spoon of sugar.

seg.f9bc03f64077.en: Our Jeedipappu cashews are whole and plain, so they fry evenly and stay crunchy against the soft rava. It is on the table in about 25 minutes. This recipe serves 3.

seg.5fe03b6066ae.en: Chop the onion, ginger and coriander leaves, slit the green chillies, and measure out the water.

seg.015e5d6ef88c.en: Roast the rava in a dry pan till it smells toasty, about 5 minutes. Keep it pale. Stir all the time on medium-low heat, then tip it onto a plate.

seg.2ccb9bbfe373.en: Heat the ghee in a wide, heavy pan on medium-low heat.

seg.827cce77ebf1.en: Fry the cashews in the ghee till golden; lift them out. This takes about 1–2 minutes; keep the ghee in the pan.

seg.57b61920de4c.en: Temper mustard, dals and curry leaves. Soften the onion and chillies, add water and salt, and boil. Let the mustard seeds splutter and the dals turn light golden before the curry leaves go in, then add the ginger with the onion and cook for 3–4 minutes till the onion is soft.

seg.be01d433ae80.en: Taste the water once it boils; it should taste a little salty, as the rava will take up the salt.

seg.b99b11495ead.en: Turn the heat to low. Pour in the rava in a thin stream, stirring. Cover on low for 3 minutes; top with the cashews.

seg.fbf1f55f7751.en: Before adding the cashews, check the upma: the rava should be soft with no hard grains, and the upma should leave the sides of the pan. If it is still grainy, sprinkle in 2 tbsp hot water, cover and cook 1 minute more.

seg.28e90add4ba6.en: Stir in the extra spoon of ghee and the coriander leaves, if using, along with most of the cashews.

seg.351e9512c914.en: Serve hot, with the rest of the cashews on top.

seg.4643e12d303d.en: Pour the rava in a thin stream while stirring so no lumps form.

seg.3c98bb62770b.en: Roasting the rava first keeps each grain separate; skip it and the upma turns sticky.

seg.fc5bc0e0bf4e.en: Fry the cashews on medium-low heat and lift them out as soon as they turn golden; they keep darkening in the hot ghee.

seg.975560a8a158.en: Upma firms up as it stands, so take it off the heat when it is a little softer than you want.

seg.508f0ab3992d.en: Vegetable upma: add ½ cup chopped carrot, beans and green peas with the onion and cook them for 3–4 minutes before the water goes in.

seg.1742d7bd0e23.en: Tomato upma: add 1 chopped tomato after the onion and cook till soft before adding the water.

seg.1981c7f3fc60.en: Godhuma rava upma: use the same amount of wheat rava with 3 cups water and cook it covered for 5–6 minutes.

seg.01300d94ad36.en: Serve hot as a breakfast tiffin with coconut chutney, allam pachadi or a spoon of sugar, or next to pesarattu for pesarattu upma.

seg.3316a3d82f44.en: Upma is best eaten hot, soon after it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and sprinkle with water before reheating.

seg.b53646711bf0.en: How do I make upma without lumps?

seg.429b54b4ab3a.en: Keep the water at a boil, turn the heat to low and pour in the rava in a thin stream with one hand while you stir with the other.

seg.0c2874233201.en: What is the right rava to water ratio for upma?

seg.91a8fe1a38a5.en: For a soft Andhra-style upma, use 2½ cups water to 1 cup bombay rava. Use 2 cups for a firmer, more separate upma.

seg.bd11a83d27d8.en: The rava was not roasted, or too much water went in. Roast the rava till it smells toasty, and stay close to 2½ cups water per cup.

seg.247181e411d9.en: When should I add cashews to upma?

seg.83f262d9c56e.en: Fry them in the ghee first and lift them out, then stir them in at the end. Added early, they turn soft in the upma.

seg.de7ddbad7bf0.en: Kobbari undalu are the coconut laddus Andhra homes make for festivals, naivedyam and an everyday sweet. They need only coconut, jaggery, cardamom and a spoon of ghee. The jaggery is melted and strained, the coconut is cooked in it on a low flame until the mix holds together, and the laddus are rolled by hand while still warm.

seg.089fb020d00e.en: Our Cheruku Bellam gives them a light golden colour and a mellow caramel taste. This recipe makes about 14 laddus.

seg.15ef8686cc9e.en: Grate the coconut, leaving out the brown skin so the laddus stay light in colour.

seg.00b442d7f507.en: Pound or grate the cane jaggery into small pieces so it melts evenly.

seg.c25e0610c714.en: Melt the jaggery with 2 tbsp water on a low flame, then strain it through a fine sieve. This catches any grit or bits of cane from the block.

seg.3eb20f2a7136.en: Return it to the pan, add the coconut and cook on medium-low, stirring, until the mix leaves the sides of the pan and holds together, 12–15 minutes. Keep stirring so it does not catch at the bottom.

seg.e1985b8e5f9c.en: If you are using cashews, fry them in a little ghee till golden while the mix cooks.

seg.1dc27e2d9b3e.en: Stir in the cardamom, ghee and cashews. Take the pan off the heat.

seg.d4ee96780aba.en: Let it cool till you can handle it, grease your palms with ghee and roll it into small balls. Press each one firmly so it holds together.

seg.3753ea8bc7d0.en: Set the laddus on a greased plate and let them cool completely before you store them.

seg.fb3de84de9f6.en: If the mix won't hold a shape, cook it 2 minutes more. If it sets too hard, sprinkle in a spoon of warm milk and press again.

seg.71475e1a7345.en: Keep the flame at medium-low; on a high flame the jaggery darkens and the laddus turn hard.

seg.46a2e2b2d323.en: Roll the laddus while the mix is still warm; once it cools completely it will not bind.

seg.b277c024adad.en: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for darker laddus with a slightly smoky sweetness.

seg.7b597df04222.en: Dry coconut: use the same amount of grated dry coconut (kopra); the mix comes together faster, so watch it closely.

seg.676bca051e10.en: Kobbari burfi: spread the cooked mix on a greased plate, let it set a little and cut it into squares instead of rolling laddus.

seg.80538d77ab41.en: Serve as an everyday sweet, offer them as naivedyam, or add them to the festival sweet plate.

seg.6f3252f28ef8.en: Keep in an airtight container and eat within 3 days at room temperature, or within a week if kept in the fridge.

seg.f232fb960e89.en: Why are my kobbari undalu not holding shape?

seg.1cf59b528a13.en: The mix needs a little more cooking. Put it back on a low flame for 2 minutes, stirring, until it leaves the sides of the pan, then roll it while it is still warm.

seg.9371fa8705cd.en: Why did my laddus turn hard?

seg.ee988ba3472f.en: The jaggery was cooked too long or on too high a flame. Sprinkle in a spoon of warm milk, mix and press again. Next time, take the pan off the heat as soon as the mix holds together.

seg.d830316a6adb.en: Can I make kobbari undalu with palm jaggery?

seg.813bf680c8a8.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The laddus turn darker, with a slightly smoky sweetness.

seg.ea6121eb3993.en: How long do kobbari undalu keep?

seg.26aba27412dc.en: About 3 days in an airtight container at room temperature, and up to a week in the fridge.

seg.992a8475993f.en: Kodi vepudu is the dry Andhra chicken fry: small pieces of chicken cooked in their own juices, then fried hard in oil with curry leaves, green chillies and a just-roasted masala until dark and sticky with spice. It is the starter at Andhra weddings and the side that sits next to rasam rice or pappu at home.

seg.db90598234ea.en: Our Teja chilli powder gives it the deep red colour and the heat Andhra fries are known for, our turmeric powder goes into the marinade, and our whole cashew kernels, fried golden, go in at the end. Serves 4 as a side.

seg.8df3bc4567e3.en: Pat the chicken dry with a cloth so the marinade sticks.

seg.075327f4deca.en: Marinate the chicken in Teja chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt, 30 minutes. Mix well with your hands so every piece is coated.

seg.63af904bba96.en: Meanwhile, dry-roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, cloves and cinnamon in a small pan on low heat until fragrant and a shade darker, about 2 minutes. Cool and grind to a coarse powder. This is the fry masala.

seg.4406ac2e72fe.en: Put the chicken in a heavy kadai with no water, cover and set it on medium heat.

seg.93ccca0c5178.en: Cook it covered in its own juices till no pink remains, about 12 minutes. Stir once or twice; the chicken releases water as it cooks.

seg.32f3a3f56679.en: Uncover and cook on high, stirring, until the liquid has almost dried up, 3–4 minutes. Tip the chicken out onto a plate and wipe the kadai.

seg.f3e846aa4edd.en: Heat the oil in the kadai on medium heat.

seg.e210c9534a07.en: Fry the cashews in oil till golden; lift out. They take under a minute, so stir them all the time and lift them out with a slotted spoon.

seg.09e282d2e36f.en: Add the onion, if using, and fry until golden. Fry the green chillies and curry leaves. Stand back; the leaves crackle and spit.

seg.1fae224eb27a.en: Add the chicken and fry masala. Fry on high till dry and dark, then toss in the cashews. Keep tossing for 6–8 minutes, until the masala clings to the pieces and the edges turn dark and crisp.

seg.0b62f402945c.en: Taste, add salt if needed, scatter the coriander leaves and serve hot.

seg.349c72ce839a.en: Fry it on high heat at the end so the masala clings to every piece.

seg.d287ba2c2c11.en: Teja chilli powder is very hot. For medium heat use 1 tsp, or swap in Sannam chilli powder for the red colour with less fire.

seg.a0ef9b138cd4.en: Cut the pieces small and even so they cook through at the same time and crisp up well in the fry.

seg.d72b3c1c529a.en: Grind the fry masala just before you cook; the roasted spice smell is the soul of a good vepudu.

seg.62d6684e446e.en: Bone-in: use 600 g small bone-in pieces and cook them in their juices for 18–20 minutes, until no pink remains near the bone.

seg.6960fe7f3ff8.en: Kobbari vepudu: add 3 tbsp grated dry coconut to the fry with the masala and toss until it browns.

seg.b4d28033bb05.en: Mutton vepudu: pressure-cook 500 g boneless mutton with the marinade and ½ cup water for 5–6 whistles, until tender, then fry it the same way.

seg.2c4ab1a1a5de.en: Serve hot as a side with rasam rice, pappu and rice or sambar rice, or on its own as a starter with sliced onion and lemon wedges.

seg.b7598301bd86.en: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan with a few drops of oil until steaming hot all the way through; it crisps up again.

seg.551573b4b443.en: What is the difference between chicken fry and chicken curry in Andhra?

seg.dbeff7335e31.en: Vepudu is dry: the chicken is cooked in its own juices, then fried until the masala coats it with no gravy. Kodi kura is a curry with an onion-tomato gravy for rice.

seg.439aacfe8e34.en: Should I use boneless or bone-in chicken for vepudu?

seg.04112853a660.en: Both work. Boneless cooks faster and crisps more; small bone-in pieces have more flavour but need 6–8 minutes longer in their juices.

seg.ade697e78f9b.en: Cut open the thickest piece. The chicken is cooked when no pink remains in the middle (or near the bone) and the juices run clear.

seg.eddd3046275b.en: How do I make kodi vepudu less spicy?

seg.9b5459aec9d6.en: Use 1 tsp Teja chilli powder, or swap in Sannam chilli powder, and slit only 2 green chillies. The cashews and curry leaves keep the flavour full.

seg.f9771e2222df.en: Nimmakaya pulihora is the bright yellow lemon rice of Andhra homes: cooked rice tossed with a crackling tempering of peanuts, chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, green chillies and curry leaves, then soured with lemon juice. It is the rice packed for train journeys, school tiffin boxes and temple days, and it is made in big batches for festivals and pujas.

seg.ac569e0882d5.en: Our turmeric powder goes into the hot oil for a few seconds, which turns every grain an even golden yellow and takes away its raw edge. This recipe serves 4.

seg.bc63d9715c03.en: Wash the rice and cook it with 2 cups of water until just done, so the grains stay separate. You need about 3 cups of cooked rice.

seg.adb2b75edafc.en: Spread the cooked rice on a plate to cool; add the salt. Fluff it with a fork and let it sit about 10 minutes until warm, not hot, so the grains do not break when mixed.

seg.e05322a3ed24.en: Heat the oil; fry the peanuts, dals, mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves. Start with the peanuts on medium heat and fry them about 2 minutes until they crackle and the skins darken.

seg.542a4fea7b18.en: Add the chana dal and urad dal and fry until light golden, about 1 minute.

seg.502483d7a042.en: Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add the dry red chillies, green chillies, ginger and curry leaves and fry a few seconds until the leaves turn crisp.

seg.6e856356980b.en: Stir in the turmeric powder and hing; switch off. Stir for 5–10 seconds only so the turmeric cooks in the hot oil without burning.

seg.dd6ccaf923d8.en: Pour over the rice, add the lemon juice and mix gently. Use your fingers or a flat spatula and lift the rice from below so every grain turns yellow without turning mushy.

seg.1bfc2c04d40e.en: Taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed. The rice should taste clearly sour and salty, as the flavour softens on standing.

seg.8cea6688d0fb.en: Cover and rest the pulihora for 15 minutes before serving so the rice takes in the lemon and tempering.

seg.c1a7043ce357.en: Add the lemon juice off the heat so it stays sharp. Cooked lemon juice turns bitter.

seg.b634a4257b6c.en: Cook the rice slightly firm and let it cool before mixing; hot, soft rice turns pasty.

seg.a1d93274ea3f.en: Keep the turmeric powder in the oil for just a few seconds; burnt turmeric gives a dark colour and a bitter taste.

seg.747474140bbf.en: Leftover rice from the morning works well, as the grains are already firm and separate.

seg.7a379d805448.en: Cashews: fry 10 cashew halves with the peanuts for a festive pulihora.

seg.be93899ec308.en: Mamidikaya pulihora: in place of lemon juice, mix in 1 cup grated raw mango with the tempering.

seg.867dba923c04.en: Grated coconut: add 2 tbsp grated coconut along with the lemon juice for a milder rice.

seg.88b87529b506.en: Serve at room temperature with curd, a pickle or appadams. It is a classic tiffin-box and travel rice.

seg.d20a641bec03.en: Pack it for a lunch box or a short journey and eat it within about 4 hours. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them within a day.

seg.c12ab7274709.en: Why does my lemon rice taste bitter?

seg.bc9078e02646.en: Either the lemon juice was cooked or the turmeric burnt in the oil. Add the turmeric last, switch off the stove right after and stir for only 5–10 seconds; add the lemon juice to the rice, off the heat.

seg.69e4bfb93ba8.en: What is the difference between pulihora and lemon rice?

seg.f2f993f1b94b.en: Pulihora is the Telugu name for soured rice. Chintapandu pulihora is soured with tamarind paste; nimmakaya pulihora is the lemon version, quicker to make and lighter in colour.

seg.1ab5dcf1d80a.en: How do I stop lemon rice from getting mushy?

seg.8a0fad2d4bfd.en: Cook the rice a little firm with less water, cool it on a plate, and mix gently by lifting from below instead of pressing.

seg.dd00224f5f94.en: How much lemon juice for 3 cups of rice?

seg.50f8efabb87e.en: About 3 tbsp, the juice of 2 medium lemons. Add it slowly and taste, because lemons vary in sourness.

seg.4b090c2ce3d3.en: Filter coffee is how many Telugu homes start the day: a strong decoction dripped through a steel filter, topped up with hot milk and frothed between a tumbler and davara. This version is sweetened with grated palm jaggery (thati bellam) in place of sugar.

seg.cff6d2079da1.en: Palm jaggery gives the cup a deep, slightly smoky caramel sweetness that sits well with the bitterness of the decoction. Once the decoction is ready it takes about 5 minutes, and it suits a slow morning as much as an evening break.

seg.95d91fecafcb.en: Make the decoction: put 2 tbsp filter coffee powder in the top chamber of a South Indian coffee filter, set the perforated press on it and pour in ½ cup water just off the boil. Cover and leave it to drip for 10–15 minutes.

seg.9024c8716b54.en: While it drips, grate the palm jaggery finely so it dissolves in seconds.

seg.24689e3dd311.en: Pour the milk into a small saucepan and set it on medium heat.

seg.4d8e3042dc81.en: Bring the milk to a boil. As soon as it froths up the sides of the pan, switch off the heat.

seg.a124a0d34983.en: Pour the decoction into a tumbler and add the hot milk. Use 2 tbsp decoction for a mild cup and 3 tbsp for a strong one.

seg.85570720618b.en: Let it stand for about a minute, so the milk is just off the boil.

seg.eacea0d7cf43.en: Stir in the palm jaggery off the heat. Keep stirring for 20–30 seconds, until no grains are left at the bottom of the tumbler.

seg.08b600da2ef8.en: Taste, and add a little more jaggery if you like it sweeter.

seg.878b0d8d7eeb.en: Pour between tumbler and davara to froth. Hold the tumbler high and pour into the davara, then back again, 3–4 times, until a light foam sits on top.

seg.653390b95f57.en: Serve straight away, in the tumbler set inside the davara.

seg.33aca43ebf99.en: Add jaggery after the milk is off the boil so it does not split.

seg.60404da43771.en: Grate the jaggery finely: fine shreds dissolve in seconds, while lumps sink and stay at the bottom of the tumbler.

seg.ca883342300e.en: Palm jaggery has a deep, slightly smoky sweetness, so start with 1 tsp and add more to taste.

seg.d7c0084f5cc6.en: A steel tumbler and davara keep the coffee hot and make frothing easy; a mug and a jug work too.

seg.1b917ac5fc8c.en: Cane jaggery: use the same amount of grated cane jaggery for a lighter, caramel-like sweetness.

seg.0ada954bebfe.en: Palm jaggery tea: make your usual milk tea, switch off the heat, wait a minute, then stir in the palm jaggery the same way.

seg.6512d133d4c0.en: No coffee filter: dissolve 1 tsp instant coffee in 2 tbsp hot water and use it in place of the decoction.

seg.e9e80ce83cf6.en: Serve hot after a breakfast of idli, dosa or upma, or in the evening with biscuits or murukulu.

seg.97817ad1f29f.en: Make each cup as you need it; coffee reheated after the jaggery goes in can split. Keep extra decoction covered at room temperature and use it within the day.

seg.ea4f4072538a.en: Why did my coffee curdle when I added palm jaggery?

seg.180a2670ead3.en: Jaggery stirred into milk that is still boiling can make it split. Take the milk off the heat, let it stand for about a minute, then stir in the grated jaggery.

seg.2b9449407096.en: Can I use cane jaggery instead of palm jaggery?

seg.890ae3e15593.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery. The coffee tastes lighter and more like caramel, while palm jaggery gives a deeper, slightly smoky cup.

seg.e4c92d1c8a42.en: How much palm jaggery should I add to one cup of coffee?

seg.43a5dfb10340.en: 1 to 2 tsp of grated palm jaggery for 1 cup of milk and 2 tbsp of decoction. Start with 1 tsp, taste, and add more if you like.

seg.2ba4fb9452bb.en: Can I make palm jaggery coffee without a coffee filter?

seg.23f63da2d908.en: Yes. Dissolve 1 tsp instant coffee in 2 tbsp hot water, use it in place of the decoction and follow the same steps.

seg.1143d51ba236.en: Paramannam is the rice-and-milk sweet that Telugu homes cook for festivals and pujas: rice simmered slowly in milk until soft and creamy, then sweetened. Bellam paramannam, made with jaggery, is a common naivedyam at Diwali, Sankranti and Varalakshmi Vratham, offered at the puja and then shared at the festive meal.

seg.360051f42785.en: Cane jaggery turns it a light caramel colour and gives a rounder, toffee-like sweetness. Ghee-fried cashews and a little cardamom finish it. This recipe serves 4.

seg.480e0a7d227f.en: Wash the rice in 2–3 changes of water until the water runs almost clear, then drain it well.

seg.d5b0fc46818a.en: Pour the milk into a heavy-bottomed pan and bring it to a boil on medium heat, about 8–10 minutes. Stir now and then so it does not catch at the bottom.

seg.b8f9c8c6758b.en: Add the drained rice to the boiling milk and turn the heat to low.

seg.9ae9baab76d7.en: Cook the washed rice in the milk on a low flame till soft and creamy, about 30 minutes. Stir often, scraping the bottom and sides of the pan each time.

seg.ec1509a08b4c.en: Check the rice: a grain should mash easily between your fingers, and the milk should have thickened slightly. For a creamier paramannam, lightly mash a few grains against the side of the pan.

seg.d8ba0a82f4ec.en: Switch off and let it rest 5 minutes. This brings the milk below the boil, so the jaggery will not split it.

seg.ca16c98d9b18.en: Stir in the jaggery till it melts, about 1–2 minutes, keeping the pan off the heat.

seg.74412a8cc141.en: Taste, and stir in a little more grated jaggery if you want it sweeter.

seg.92b56df40ea6.en: Heat the ghee in a small pan on medium-low heat.

seg.1bb1f411e4d0.en: Fry the cashews in ghee; add with the cardamom. Stir the cashews until golden, about 1 minute, adding the raisins for the last few seconds until they puff up. Pour the nuts and ghee into the paramannam, sprinkle in the cardamom powder and stir.

seg.e10b7192c157.en: Serve warm. Paramannam thickens as it stands; loosen it with a few spoons of warm milk, off the heat, if needed.

seg.d30196cf6b28.en: Jaggery goes in off the heat so the milk does not split.

seg.d4a9c2ee09bf.en: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and scrape the bottom each time you stir; milk catches easily during the long simmer.

seg.a01441abc0b6.en: Cook the rice until fully soft before the jaggery goes in; the grains do not soften further once it is sweetened.

seg.688b80a32383.en: Grate the jaggery finely so it melts in the hot milk without going back on the stove.

seg.7bf8faca62b8.en: Palm jaggery: use the same amount of grated palm jaggery for a darker colour and a deeper, smoky sweetness.

seg.6672d2210281.en: Pesarapappu paramannam: dry-roast 2 tbsp split moong dal until light golden, wash it and cook it with the rice.

seg.988ab75b5ccb.en: Serve warm as naivedyam at the Diwali or Lakshmi puja, then as the sweet at the festive meal. Some like it chilled the next day.

seg.4a60d211f14d.en: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days. It sets thick when chilled; stir in a little warm milk, off the heat, before serving.

seg.2949774c7efb.en: Why did my paramannam curdle after adding jaggery?

seg.283626ae50fc.en: Jaggery stirred into milk that is still on the heat or boiling can make it split. Switch off, let the paramannam rest for about 5 minutes, then stir in the grated jaggery.

seg.7df6976d1e83.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated palm jaggery (thati bellam). The paramannam turns darker and tastes deeper and slightly smoky.

seg.6ac2cfc26fb7.en: Which rice is best for paramannam?

seg.ead18bc39c32.en: A short-grain rice such as sona masoori cooks soft and creamy in milk. Long-grain basmati keeps its grains separate and gives a thinner paramannam.

seg.2baf5cc4ec36.en: How do I fix paramannam that has become too thick?

seg.9ffeabf346fa.en: Stir in a few spoons of warm milk, off the heat, until it loosens. It thickens as it cools, so stop when it is a little thinner than you want.

seg.8922ef1e3767.en: Pasupu annam is plain rice turned bright yellow with turmeric and tossed in a crackling tempering of mustard seeds, chana dal, curry leaves and green chillies, with fried cashews on top. Andhra homes make it for lunch boxes, for quick weekday meals and as a prasadam on puja days, often with the morning's leftover rice.

seg.510252086556.en: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) gives the rice its deep yellow colour and an earthy turmeric smell, so half a teaspoon is enough for 4. Whole cashews (Jeedipappu) fried in the same oil add the crunch.

seg.38badedc8d11.en: Total includes about 15 minutes for the cooked rice to cool.

seg.8ad70ebff643.en: Cook rice and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seeds, chana dal, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add hill turmeric powder and toss in the rice.

seg.53fcfe53b909.en: Wash the rice in 2–3 changes of water and drain it.

seg.cdcf37be99e8.en: Cook the rice so the grains stay separate, then spread it on a plate to cool. Use 2 cups water to 1 cup rice in a pot or pressure cooker (2 whistles), and fluff it with a fork before spreading it out.

seg.296995189451.en: Let the rice cool for about 15 minutes until it is just warm. Sprinkle the salt over it.

seg.48839bd22983.en: Heat the oil in a wide kadai on medium heat.

seg.bdc1a0df8ffc.en: Fry the cashews in the oil till golden; lift out. Add mustard seeds and chana dal. Keep the cashews on a plate; they turn golden in about 1 minute.

seg.0729c6efc94a.en: Once the mustard seeds splutter, add the urad dal and the dried red chillies and stir.

seg.2688182af66a.en: When the dal turns golden, add the chillies and curry leaves, then the turmeric on low heat. Add the ginger and asafoetida with the curry leaves, and stir the turmeric for only 5–10 seconds.

seg.59fd9b87153d.en: Switch off the heat straight away so the turmeric does not burn.

seg.15dc85e42ca1.en: Tip in the rice, cashews and salt and toss gently till evenly yellow. Use a flat spatula and lift and fold rather than pressing down, so the grains stay whole.

seg.b005e5771235.en: Taste for salt, stir in the ghee if using, cover and leave for 5 minutes before serving so the rice takes on the tempering.

seg.9bce1ed4dbee.en: Spread the rice to cool first so the grains do not break.

seg.1f9a348f8750.en: Add the turmeric on low heat and stir for only a few seconds; burnt turmeric turns the rice bitter.

seg.394d01a50207.en: Hill turmeric powder colours strongly; start with ½ tsp for 1 cup of rice and add a pinch more only if you want a deeper yellow.

seg.505872469eb9.en: Leftover rice from the morning works well, as long as the grains are separate.

seg.ab1b24f9cf3d.en: Turmeric powder: our everyday Pasupu turmeric powder works the same way; use the same ½ tsp.

seg.302f50dc74c9.en: Peanuts: fry 2 tbsp raw peanuts in the oil before the cashews for extra crunch.

seg.551f49339b3d.en: Lemon: squeeze in the juice of half a lemon with the rice for a tangy, pulihora-style rice.

seg.6b9e9c07efba.en: Coconut: toss in 2 tbsp grated coconut along with the rice.

seg.d541a1d237fc.en: Serve warm or at room temperature with curd, appadalu or a dry potato fry. It also packs well for lunch boxes and travel.

seg.db97e1ae49fa.en: Best eaten the same day. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and warm them with a sprinkle of water.

seg.54acb7b11b4c.en: How do you make pasupu annam?

seg.d99d12f26e71.en: Cook rice so the grains stay separate and let it cool. Fry cashews, mustard seeds, chana dal, chillies and curry leaves in oil, add turmeric on low heat for a few seconds, then toss in the rice with salt.

seg.a4a87b4f7d63.en: How much turmeric powder goes into turmeric rice?

seg.aa37527cdcfb.en: About ½ tsp for 1 cup of raw rice (about 3 cups cooked). Hill turmeric powder colours strongly, so start with less and add a pinch more if needed.

seg.3d200fb0e6fc.en: Why is my turmeric rice bitter?

seg.2c9da3559a42.en: The turmeric burnt in the hot oil, or too much went in. Add it on low heat, stir for only a few seconds and switch off before tipping in the rice.

seg.36ca370ac0d9.en: Can I make pasupu annam with leftover rice?

seg.71df75edcd26.en: Yes. Leftover rice with separate grains works well. Break up any lumps with your fingers before tossing it in the tempering.

seg.5fbc274b0656.en: Pasupu paalu is warm milk simmered with a little turmeric and a pinch of black pepper, then sweetened with jaggery. It is an everyday cup in many Telugu homes, made on cool evenings and often through Karthika masam, the month of Somavaram (Monday) pujas and evening lamps.

seg.7d5fe2bc79e0.en: The turmeric turns the milk golden and gives it an earthy, slightly bitter edge, the pepper adds a little heat, and the jaggery rounds it off with a caramel sweetness. This recipe makes one cup in about 5 minutes.

seg.94d57531a741.en: Add the turmeric and pepper (and the cardamom, if using) and stir until no specks of turmeric float on top. They mix in more evenly before the milk is heated.

seg.9da3932c6508.en: Set the pan on medium-low heat. Warm the milk with the turmeric and pepper; simmer 2 minutes. Once small bubbles appear around the edge, turn the heat to low and let it bubble gently.

seg.c66cb9336ef5.en: Stir now and then and keep an eye on the pan, as milk rises fast once it boils. If it starts to climb, lift the pan off the heat for a few seconds.

seg.b567bc0c93c9.en: It is ready when the milk is an even golden yellow and the raw smell of turmeric has gone.

seg.6e16c50d7c2a.en: Switch off and wait a minute. The milk drops just below the boil, so the jaggery will not split it.

seg.aa0d1bcf6802.en: For a smooth cup, pour the milk through a fine sieve into a tumbler or mug.

seg.862cac523844.en: Stir in the jaggery and serve warm. Stir for 20–30 seconds, until it dissolves, and taste for sweetness.

seg.1d9b9ec736a8.en: Strain through a fine sieve if you like it smooth.

seg.018366193ef3.en: Add the jaggery only after switching off; jaggery stirred into boiling milk can split it.

seg.0e783ba83473.en: Use a steel pan and spoon; turmeric stains plastic and wood.

seg.dc2a0c79ccd5.en: Making more? Use the same amounts for each cup of milk.

seg.485f68415013.en: Hill turmeric: use Hill Turmeric Powder (konda pasupu) in place of turmeric powder, in the same amount.

seg.01ec7a142032.en: Palm or cane jaggery: palm jaggery gives a deeper, slightly smoky sweetness; cane jaggery a lighter, caramel one.

seg.15b67235d087.en: Milder cup: leave out the pepper and add a pinch of cardamom powder instead.

seg.d80219c8a51f.en: Serve warm in a tumbler or mug, on a cool evening or after the Karthika Somavaram puja.

seg.ac04ffd1d51a.en: Make it as you need it and drink it warm. Reheating after the jaggery is in can split the milk.

seg.c758e61dd102.en: Why did my pasupu paalu curdle?

seg.d5f9c6fb2e27.en: Jaggery stirred into milk that is still boiling can make it split. Switch off the heat, wait about a minute, then stir in the grated jaggery.

seg.df4dbdd3102b.en: How much turmeric should I use for one cup of milk?

seg.3ec50124bdd7.en: ¼ tsp turmeric powder for 1 cup (about 240 ml) of milk. More than that makes the taste sharp and earthy.

seg.3dc4d1edd4f9.en: Can I skip the black pepper?

seg.166b3a44e11d.en: Yes. The pepper adds a little heat to the taste; leave it out, or use a pinch of cardamom instead, for a milder cup.

seg.2184adfd31b0.en: Should I use palm jaggery or cane jaggery?

seg.ef65c3a9d015.en: Either works, 1 tsp grated per cup. Palm jaggery tastes deeper and slightly smoky; cane jaggery is lighter and more like caramel.

seg.cc1333072822.en: Ragi java is a pourable porridge of ragi flour cooked in water, a daily drink in many Andhra and Rayalaseema homes. The salted version is made with buttermilk; this sweet one is loosened with milk and sweetened with jaggery, and it is drunk warm from a steel tumbler at breakfast or in the evening.

seg.b29ec96bcd5c.en: Our Thati Bellam palm jaggery suits the earthy taste of ragi and gives the java a toffee-brown colour. It takes about 15 minutes from start to finish. This recipe serves 2.

seg.c288f67fcabb.en: Pour the other cup of water into a heavy-bottomed pan; a thin pan lets the ragi catch.

seg.ec55acf2b96a.en: Boil the other cup of water, pour in the ragi and stir on low heat till thick and glossy, 6–8 minutes. Stir the mix once more before pouring, as the flour settles at the bottom of the bowl.

seg.d0f8efa78d43.en: Keep stirring all the time. The java is cooked when it turns from dull pinkish-brown to a darker, glossy brown and coats the back of the spoon.

seg.e7ef07a808c5.en: Add the milk and simmer 2 minutes. Switch off and rest 2 minutes. Stir once or twice while it simmers so it does not catch.

seg.8f86db3a6d08.en: Grate the palm jaggery finely while the java rests, so it melts quickly.

seg.9cad3a0176bc.en: Stir in the palm jaggery and cardamom. Serve warm. Stir till the jaggery has fully melted, then taste and add a little more if needed.

seg.a8de8fe6382d.en: Pour into tumblers or bowls. If it is too thick to drink, stir in a few spoons of warm milk.

seg.c3916a972329.en: Always mix the ragi flour in water first; flour added straight to boiling water forms lumps that do not break up.

seg.966098732312.en: Do not rush the cooking; undercooked ragi tastes raw and floury.

seg.7c0f350f3691.en: For a thinner java to drink from a tumbler, use 2 tbsp ragi flour; for a spoonable porridge, use ⅓ cup.

seg.146636ba6c2e.en: With dry fruit: stir in a few chopped cashews or almonds and a spoon of raisins at the end.

seg.6fc3ada569ad.en: Without milk: cook the ragi in 2½ cups water and stir in the jaggery once it has stopped bubbling, for a thinner, darker java.

seg.639ea388ead3.en: Serve warm in a steel tumbler or bowl for breakfast, or as an evening drink with a few biscuits or murukulu. Some like it chilled in summer.

seg.e770a9eec01e.en: Best drunk the day it is made. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day and stir in a little warm milk, off the heat, when reheating.

seg.a10b6147a5ac.en: How do I make ragi java without lumps?

seg.ca8628b7e082.en: Whisk the ragi flour into room-temperature water first until smooth, then pour this into boiling water while stirring all the time.

seg.8bd78affc52d.en: How do I know ragi java is cooked?

seg.9b05db7490cb.en: It turns darker and glossy, thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, and no longer tastes floury. This takes about 6–8 minutes on low heat.

seg.e87c26125f87.en: Can I use cane jaggery in ragi java?

seg.a9a06390a945.en: Yes. Use the same amount of grated cane jaggery (cheruku bellam) and stir it in after switching off the stove, so the milk does not split. It gives a lighter colour and a milder, caramel-like sweetness.

seg.9a71713417de.en: What is the difference between ragi java and ragi malt?

seg.c2632b6d0b4f.en: They are the same drink with different names. Ragi java is the Telugu name; ragi malt is what it is often called in shops and on menus.

seg.671d48882eed.en: Iguru is the Andhra way of cooking meat or prawns down in a thick onion masala until almost dry, so the spices cling to every piece. Royyala iguru comes from the coastal districts, from Nellore to Godavari to Srikakulam, where prawns from the backwaters and the sea are a Sunday lunch with rice.

seg.ff39877dbdbd.en: Our hill turmeric powder (Konda Pasupu) goes on the prawns first and into the masala. Teja chilli powder brings the deep red colour and strong heat coastal homes like, so scale it to your table.

seg.885826f68de3.en: Prep includes cleaning the prawns and the 10-minute rest with turmeric.

seg.cff5bbd725a6.en: Rub prawns with turmeric and salt. Fry onions and ginger-garlic paste, add Teja chilli powder and coriander powder, then cook the prawns in the masala till it coats them.
